news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire health and social care partnership running down reserves to cover funding shortfall
news_drafts.lead: The Health and Social Care Partnership serving East Dunbartonshire has depleted nearly a third of its general reserves in a single year to bridge a funding gap, with savings targets falling far short of what is needed. The partnership achieved only 39 per cent of its 2026/27 savings programme by month 4, a shortfall it is covering by drawing down £8.192m from reserves. General contingency reserves have fallen from £3.955m to a projected £1.290m by March 2027. The partnership explicitly warns that continued reliance on reserve drawdowns to balance budgets "may be compromised" its financial sustainability. The financial strain has forced service access restrictions: charges are rising, eligibility criteria tightening and waiting lists extending. A 3.5 per cent pay uplift for staff was approved with no corresponding funding, adding to the pressure. The partnership carried forward £3.036m in unachieved savings from previous years, which must still be realised alongside current targets.

news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire underlying borrowing need to reach £785m by 2028/29, cash reserves to fall to £1.7m
news_drafts.lead: East Dunbartonshire's underlying borrowing need, the total the council has spent on long-lived assets it has not yet paid for, will grow by 39 per cent over three years to £785m by 2028/29, according to the council's treasury management strategy. The council is currently using cash balances to bridge the gap between what it owes and what it needs to borrow. However, that buffer will shrink by 94 per cent, from £27.6m to £1.7m by 2028/29, as capital spending on housing and other programmes accelerates. Once reserves are exhausted, the council will need to borrow for all new capital expenditure. The forecast reflects a sharp increase in housing investment, with Housing Revenue Account capital spending peaking at £86.4m in 2027/28, more than five times the £16m spent in 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Interim Report 2026/27
findings.headline: The council repaid a £1,000,000 market loan carrying an interest rate of 10.94% on 7 April 2026.
findings.detail: The repayments table records this as a market deal repaid on the same day it was listed. It is the only market loan in the repayments table.
findings.matters: Retiring a loan at a rate of almost 11% removes one of the council's highest-cost borrowings, which is relevant to peers reviewing legacy high-rate debt.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Interim Report 2026/27
findings.headline: The council repaid £93,096,287.70 of principal from 1 April to 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The repayments table includes PWLB loans, temporary deals and one market loan. The total principal repaid is shown at the foot of the table.
findings.matters: Repayments of this size are the cash the council had to find in the half-year, and they set the replacement funding it had to arrange.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Interim Report 2026/27
findings.headline: Temporary deals taken in September 2026 carried interest rates of 4.60% to 4.80%, compared with 4.05% to 4.20% on some deals taken in June 2026.
findings.detail: The rates on the new temporary deals rose over the period. The PWLB loans taken in August and September 2026 carried rates of 4.55%, 4.67% and 4.95%.
findings.matters: A rise in the rate on new short-term borrowing raises the council's cost of funds, and peer councils and lenders would want to see the same trend in their own figures.
findings.figures: Temporary deals at 4.05% and 4.20% (June 2026); 4.80% and 4.60% (September 2026); PWLB loans at 4.55%, 4.67% and 4.95%

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Interim Report 2026/27
findings.headline: The council took on £112,000,000 of new borrowing from 1 April to 30 September 2026, in a mix of temporary deals and three PWLB loans.
findings.detail: The new borrowing table lists temporary deals of various sizes and three PWLB loans of £5,000,000 each. The paper gives a total of £112,000,000 for the new borrowing.
findings.matters: The scale of new borrowing and its reliance on short-term temporary deals shows how the council is funding its position, which matters to lenders and to peer councils facing similar funding conditions.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Interim Report 2026/27
findings.headline: East Dunbartonshire's external borrowing rose from £426,508,970 to £445,412,682.52 between 1 April and 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The paper records a net increase in external borrowing of £18,903,712.3 over the half-year. The closing balance at 30 September 2026 is shown as £445,412,682.52.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender can see the council's total debt grew over the first half of the year, which bears on its future funding needs.
findings.figures: Opening external borrowing £426,508,970; net increase £18,903,712.3; closing external borrowing £445,412,682.52
